For the condition to hold for every natural \(y\), \(x\) must divide the first values:
\[
F(1)=7+12-1=18,\qquad F(2)=49+24-1=72.
\]
Thus \(x\mid \gcd(18,72)=18\), so \(x\le 18\) and \(x\mid 18\).

Now check \(x=18\). Since \(7^y \pmod{18}\) has period \(3\):
\[
7^y\equiv 
\begin{cases}
1 \pmod{18}, & y\equiv 0\pmod 3,\\
7 \pmod{18}, & y\equiv 1\pmod 3,\\
13 \pmod{18}, & y\equiv 2\pmod 3.
\end{cases}
\]
Then:
- If \(y\equiv 0\pmod 3\), \(7^y+12y-1\equiv 1+0-1\equiv 0\pmod{18}\).
- If \(y\equiv 1\pmod 3\), \(7^y+12y-1\equiv 7+12-1\equiv 18\equiv 0\pmod{18}\).
- If \(y\equiv 2\pmod 3\), \(7^y+12y-1\equiv 13+24-1\equiv 36\equiv 0\pmod{18}\).

So \(18\) works. Since no valid \(x\) can exceed \(18\), the greatest is

\[
\boxed{18}
\]
